newsitem.title: USA: US says no jet fuel tenders seen for Desert Strike.
newsitem.headline: US says no jet fuel tenders seen for Desert Strike.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Defense does not expect to issue any tenders for jet fuel as a result of recent military activities near Iraq, a spokeswoman said.

"Any fuel consumption that is currently being used by the war fighter missions in Iraq are strictly within our normal consumption levels," said Marilyn Miller, public affairs officer for the Defense Fuel Supply Center (DFSC), which buys fuel for the U.S. armed services.

"(Those in charge of buying) have not been advised that there is going to be any increase in fuel consumption at the present time and they have no idea about going out for additional tenders," she added.
The U.S. fired 44 missiles at military targets in Iraq this week, in response to Saddam Hussein's refusal to halt assaults on Kurds in northern Iraq and withdraw his troops.
Iraq's troops have since complied and withdrawn.
During operations Desert Shield and Desert Storm in 1990 and 1991, the U.S. issued two tenders to buy more than five million barrels of jet fuel.
The recent skirmishes were dwarfed by that effort, when allied forces consumed more than 750,000 barrels of jet fuel a day, military sources said then.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
